messages:
noah: hey folks, got my Windows laptop (Surface Pro) but Autopilot didn't finish. laptop booted to desktop but Intune shows no device and BitLocker is on with no recovery key in portal. any idea? :confused:

it-bot: New device check: noah-device-1774509999 registered. Autopilot enrollment status: not-complete. BitLocker status: enabled locally, recovery key missing in Intune.

itops-windows: welcome noah. quick q: did the device come pre-provisioned (Autopilot) or did you set it up manually?

noah: the box just had a sticker "Autopilot ready" but i followed the OOBE prompts and signed in with my SSO. it landed on desktop and i could use it. didn't ask for company portal or enroll device flow.

jen: that sounds like Autopilot didn't claim the device UUID against our tenant. vendor sometimes skips the final registration step. can you open an elevated PowerShell and run:

```powershell
(Get-WmiObject -Namespace root\cimv2\mdm -Class MDM_Enrollment) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
```

and paste anything that looks like an EnrollmentID? don't paste secrets.

noah: pasted output: EnrollmentID : 
               00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

itops-windows: yep that zero GUID indicates it never completed MDM enrollment. Because BitLocker turned on during OOBE the recovery key got escrowed to the local TPM but not uploaded to Intune. we'll need to reprovision.

max: two options: 1) we can re-run Autopilot/Intune enrollment from within Windows and upload key, or 2) remote wipe and reprovision via Autopilot (preferred for company devices). which do you prefer?

noah: i'd rather not lose my initial config if possible. can we enroll without wiping?

itops-windows: we can try manual enrollment first: install Company Portal, sign in, then in admin center trigger a sync to upload BitLocker key. steps:
1) open Edge -> https://portal.manage.microsoft.com and download Company Portal MSI (Work or School -> Company Portal).
2) install and sign in with SSO.
3) open an elevated cmd and run `dsregcmd /status` then `dsregcmd /join` if needed.
4) in Company Portal open Devices -> click Sync. After sync, check Intune console for the device and BitLocker key escrow.

noah: installing Company Portal now. signed in and clicked sync.

it-bot: Company Portal sign-in detected for noah-device-1774509999. Sync requested.

jen: give it a few minutes. if BitLocker key still doesn't appear, run the clear-key & forced escrow steps from elevated PowerShell: first get the protector id:

```powershell
manage-bde -protectors -get c:
```

then run:

```powershell
manage-bde -protectors -adbackup c: -id <ID>
```

This attempts to backup to AD/Intune. We'll watch the Intune portal logs.

noah: manage-bde output shows a TPM protector and a numerical ID. ran the adbackup command and it returned "Key backup successful".

it-bot: Key escrow event logged. Intune shows a new recovery key pending for device-1774509999.

max: nice. i'll verify in the portal... confirmed recovery key now present and device shows as "Enrolled (MDM)". we'll clear the temporary policy that blocked some enterprise apps and push the company certs.

noah: perfect. a couple extra asks: 1) how do i enable WSL2 + Virtualization? 2) will i get admin rights to install Docker Desktop and dev tools?

itops-windows: WSL2 instructions: run PowerShell as admin and enable features:

```powershell
wsl --install -d Ubuntu
# or
Enable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName VirtualMachinePlatform,Microsoft-Windows-Subsystem-Linux -All
Restart-Computer
```

For admin rights: we provide temporary local admin for 3 days by default on Windows loaners. file a self-service request in Company Portal -> Request Admin Access if you need more time.

devex: i've noted a doc update: remind new-hires to wait for "Company-managed" OOBE screen before creating a local account or signing with personal accounts. we'll add a step to verify Intune enrollment before adding personal data.

noah: thanks all, reboots done, WSL installed and Docker runs under my account. appreciate the quick help :rocket:

itops-windows: closing loop — will keep the device marked as Autopilot reprovisioned to our tenant so vendor errors don't repeat. thanks for reporting.

max: pro tip for others: if a device boots to desktop but you expected Autopilot, check `dsregcmd /status` first to confirm join/enroll state. saves a lot of time.
